To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the herbicide molinates inhibits the growth and metabolic activity of the Streptomyces strain M2.
the herbicide molimate inhibits growth, but not the ATP synthesis of the strain M3, while the strain M2 is not affected in the growth, but the ATP synthesis is affected.
the herbicide molunate was cometabolically degraded by the microorganism S. griseus M2, which was classified on the basis on the presence of the enzyme SF‐420.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the herbicide on the metabolism of a degradating strain of Streptomyces sp. and with the possible role of SF‐420 cofactor in molinate degradation.
a new approach for the bioremediation of the herbicide, which involves a cometabolic process with a Streptomyces strain.
the effects of a xenobiotic on the metabolic activities and the production of the coenzyme SF‐421 in the strain S. griseus M2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
molinate, at the concentrations used, does not affect the final metabolic activities of S. griseus, but it may be a selective agent for the production of the cofactor SF‐ 420.

the strain M2 is able to metabolize molinate in a cometabolic way, with no apparent toxic effect on its metabolic activities, but with a progressive delay of its onset, and a progressive increase of the production of the coenzyme SF‐421.

the herbicide molinated does not exert any toxic effects on the metabolic activities and the growth of the strain M3, but exerts a toxic effect on the growth of the Streptomyces sp., M2 strain, while it stimulates SF‐420 production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of the herbicide does not affect the final growth yield of the strain, but it decreases its growth rate, and the synthesis of the cofactor SF‐421.

the strain M2 is able to degrade molinate in cometabolism, but this process is not coupled to ATP synthesis, and that the presence of molinate in high concentrations in the medium increases the production of coenzyme SF 420.
molinate, a known inhibitor of the enzyme acetyl‐CoA synthase (Acs), does not seem to affect the final synthesis of the coenzyme SF‐421, which is also a derivative of acetyl‐Co A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
molinate, which has been shown to be a toxic compound for several microbial strains, does not affect growth and metabolic activity of a degradating Streptomyces strain.
molinate, at concentrations of 100 and 200 mg L ^{−1}, is not toxic to the microorganism, and that the presence of this herbicide does not affect the synthesis of SF‐420, but it delays its onset.
, in spite of the toxicity of the herbicide, the metabolic activities of S. griseus were not inhibited.
